title: JIT sandwich of topUp / pullAndRefresh captures disproportionate share of inflow-triggered rate bump
impact: Searchers extract a slice of every rate-bumping inflow proportional to `(searcher_stake / (totalStaked + searcher_stake)) * (new_rate - old_rate) * held_duration`. Per-sandwich loss is small (e.g. 540-day window + 540e18 top-up + 10x-totalStaked searcher + 12s hold ≈ 1.25e14 wei = 0.000125 phUSD), but it repeats on every top-up and every large dispatcher drain. Scales with top-up size and searcher inventory.
proof:
1. Owner submits `topUp(large_amount)` via public mempool.
2. Searcher front-runs with `stake(X)`. `_syncBudget` runs; searcher's `user.amount = X`, `rewardDebt` snapshots current `accRewardPerShare`.
3. Owner's `topUp` lands. `rewardBudget` grows, `rewardRate` jumps, `windowEnd` resets.
4. Next block: searcher back-runs with `unstake(X)` + `claim()`. `_updatePool` accrues at new higher rate; searcher captures pro-rata of that accrual.
5. Net profit = `X / (totalStaked + X) * new_rate * elapsed`. For X >> totalStaked, searcher captures most of the first-block emission post-topUp.
suggested-fix:
Introduce a minimum stake duration or cooldown between stake and unstake (e.g. forfeit rewards for the first N seconds of a new stake, returning forfeit to `rewardBudget`). Alternatively, route owner top-ups through a private mempool / commit-reveal path. At minimum document that top-ups are MEV-visible.

Note: adopting the F-01 structural fix (amortise inflow into remaining window instead of resetting) materially reduces the sandwich surface because the rate no longer JUMPS on top-ups — it smoothly increases.
consolidation-note: No CS overlap. Standalone MEV observation from econ-scanner.
sanitizer-note: REMOVED. (1) The `ownerOrNotGriefed` modifier explicitly permits rate-increasing resets — so the rate-bump behavior is the intended design, not a bug; (2) The sandwich requires the searcher to hold BalancerPooler ERC1155 inventory at ≥10x totalStaked for meaningful extraction (the finding's own worst-case is ~0.000125 phUSD per sandwich — dust); (3) Stakers whose rate is INCREASED by a topUp suffer no harm: the sandwicher diluting that rate is a zero-sum allocation among concurrent stakers, not a theft; (4) The user has no ACTION required when topUp happens — rates are externally set — so standard 'user signed a tx that got sandwiched' MEV patterns don't cleanly apply. C4 treats this kind of speculative low-magnitude MEV on permissioned rate adjustments as non-HM without a demonstrated exploit of material value. Recommending removal rather than demotion because the behavior is spec-permitted and per-event profit is sub-cent.
